free_tier.stated: Per the tracker: EUR 5.90/month for 1 Intel core, 3072 MB RAM, 35 GB NVMe, 2560 GB/month on a 10 Gbps port, IPv4 plus IPv6, Vienna, Austria. A second EUR 5.90 row on the same page is an Epyc core with 50 GB NVMe in Vienna, and a third is the same 3 GB / 35 GB / 2560 GB shape in Amsterdam.

egress.terms: 2560 GB a month on the recorded row and 76800 GB on the largest plan, with no overage price published on the pages read

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: the vendor page states 'REST API & CLI'; panel at panel.pipehost.net; OS templates plus custom ISO; daily backups included on every plan per the page; regions selected per order with live latency measurement in the browser
chaining: EUR 5.90 for 3 GB of RAM and 35 GB of NVMe with 2.5 TB on a 10 Gbps port in Vienna is the fastest port per euro, and with the REST API and CLI it is the easiest to automate of the small hosts here. The 2.5 TB cap, not the port, is what stops it being a transfer host.

limits.value: 2560 GB a month on the recorded row against a 10 Gbps port; the largest plan on the tracker page carries 76800 GB a month. A 10 Gbps port with a 2.5 TB allowance is a burst shape: the allowance is exhausted in about 35 minutes of full-rate transfer by arithmetic, so the port is not usable as sustained throughput.
